📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-07-04-miurl-5xx-monitor-noise`
This is occurrence #8 (backlog catch-up cycle, ~8-day gap since last poll).
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `vae`
Playbook: 1) Confirm shape: monitor 302048068 in Warn/Alert, name '[VAE][miurl][P1] 5xx error rate elevated'. 2) Run sum:trace.aspnet.request.errors{service:miurl,env:prod}.as_count() and the matching .hits query over the trigger window -- if absolute errors are single digits against low sparse traffic (not hundreds), this is the known noise pattern. 3) Confirm service:miurl status:error env:prod in DD Logs returns 0 (both documented occurrences did; legacy-miurl-api does not appear to be DD-Logs-instrumented). 4) If the metric shows a genuine high-volume 5xx burst (tens+ of errors, sustained), treat as a real incident and do not apply this KB entry. 5) Owning team is ambiguous -- ownership.md maps MiURL to Transactions, but the DD monitor's own tag says team:vae; note both when reporting, same unresolved gap as the sibling miurl-agent KB entry.
Open Jira: n/a

  • miurl 5xx-rate monitor noise (existing KI, monitoring-noise-suspected-unconfirmed).

📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-07-09-ms-authentication-api-p95-latency-sustained-noerrors`
This is occurrence #2 (backlog catch-up cycle, ~8-day gap since last poll).
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `admin`
Playbook: 1) Confirm shape: monitor 299551532 in Alert (or recently Alert, now OK); re-query p95:trace.aspnet_core.request{service:ms-authentication-api,env:prod} over a wide (+/-1h) window at native granularity (NOT just the monitor's own last_10m eval) -- if breach points span 30+ minutes (not a single-point blip), this is the pattern to watch. 2) ALWAYS independently check trace.redis.command.errors{env:prod} for the SAME window before assuming this is Redis-driven, even though monitors/299551532 appears in the Redis-timeout KB's match list -- confirm actual temporal overlap, not just same-day co-occurrence. 3) Confirm 0 errors via service:ms-authentication-api status:error in DD Logs -- if errors ARE present, this is a different, more serious incident (auth failures, not just latency) and should be escalated immediately, not filed under this entry. 4) If repo access is restored, check ms-authentication-api and its immediate SQL/Mongo/Redis dependencies for a deploy or capacity change correlated with the spike start time. 5) If this recurs with the same no-error, no-Redis-correlation shape, bump occurrence count -- but given this is a critical-path service with no identified root cause, do NOT downgrade the escalation score on recurrence the way monitor-noise entries do; each occurrence should get independent Redis-correlation and error-rate verification, not just occurrence-count bumping.
Open Jira: n/a

Evidence:

📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-07-06-signup-low-traffic-p90-latency-monitor-noise`
This is occurrence #10 (backlog catch-up cycle, ~8-day gap since last poll).
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `first-strike`
Playbook: 1) Confirm shape: DD metric p90:trace.aspnet.request{env:prod,service:signup,resource_name:post_/*} in the alert window -- expect only 1-3 non-zero points (low traffic) with one point near/above 12s. 2) Confirm no errors: service:signup status:error DD Logs should be 0 (or ES fields.dd_service.keyword:signup/method-signup-ui 0 error-level hits). 3) Do not treat as an incident on a single occurrence -- self-recovers within one eval window every time so far. 4) Recommend to Growth/owning team: either raise the threshold, switch to a minimum-sample-count-gated check, or use a longer rollup window so a single slow request can't dominate p90 on a low-traffic endpoint (same monitor-noise shape as ki-2026-07-04-ms-account-api-4xx-spike-monitor-noise). 5) If a future occurrence shows >1 concurrent errors or coincides with a broader infra event (SQL cluster, gateway), treat as a genuine correlated incident instead of noise -- cross-check the SQL-cluster-cascade KB candidate referenced in the 2026-07-06T11:20:00Z team-incident-response investigation before dismissing.
Open Jira: n/a

📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-06-18-rainforest-webhook-inactive-account-500`
This is occurrence #5 (backlog catch-up cycle, ~8-day gap since last poll).
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `transactions`
Playbook: 1) Confirm via DD monitor 295882867 + APM trace.aspnet_core.request.errors{service:runtime-core-api,resource_name:*rainforest*}. 2) Confirm mechanism in ES: query "/api/v1/payments/rainforest/events" level:Error — exception.Type should be AccountNotActiveException. 3) Fix: in ProcessRainforestWebhookAsync add a `catch (AccountNotActiveException)` that logs Warning and returns Ok() (webhook already persisted; retry can never succeed for an inactive account). See fix_template. 4) Consider the same non-retryable-ack pattern for other permanent failures (account not found, deserialization) so Svix doesn't retry-storm. 5) Optionally have ExtractAccountIdFromRainforestWebhookAsync / a pre-check short-circuit inactive accounts before InitAsync.

📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-07-03-ms-scheduler-api-seriesid-negative-recordid`
This is occurrence #143 (backlog catch-up cycle, ~8-day gap since last poll).
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `crm`
Playbook: 1) Confirm shape: DD monitor 302054543 in 'Alert' state, OR ES query fields.dd_service.keyword:"ms-scheduler-api" AND fields.Account.keyword:"lafittesseafood" returning the 'Failed to Get Series Id for record -1' signature. 2) Compute the error-rate ratio in DD (errors/hits over the alert's own last_10m window) -- historically marginal (~2.5%), not a severe spike; do not over-escalate on the DD monitor state alone. 3) The root cause is a code-level missing-guard bug in SeriesDataProvider.GetSeriesIdAsync (not account-specific) -- as of 2026-07-03T21:08Z it has reproduced across 6 distinct accounts, not just lafittesseafood. Still not infra-wide (no elevated volume, no user-facing impact beyond scattered per-account 500s), but do not describe it as single-account going forward. 4) File/bump a defect for CRM Experience (#team-customer-management) rather than re-diagnosing from scratch each cycle.

🚨 *new alert — needs human*  (score: 5)
Channel: alert-system (DD-scan-diff, backlog catch-up)  •  alerts in group: 1
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `admin`

Symptoms:
  - Unlike most other fires this cycle, this one shows GENUINE slow requests (up to ~7s), not just a low-traffic ratio artifact -- several points cluster between 11:00-11:16Z reaching multi-second latency.
  - 0 corroborating error logs -- requests were slow, not failing.

📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-07-06-tables-fields-redis-circuitbreaker-p95-latency`
This is occurrence #8 (backlog catch-up cycle, ~8-day gap since last poll).
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `runtime`
Playbook: 1) Confirm shape: DD monitor 299251779 and/or 302103451 in Alert or recently-recovered state, service tables-fields. 2) Run the evidence_query in ES for 'Redis Cache Circuit Breaker OPENED' -- if present, this is the Redis-driven latency pattern, not the FieldTableNameRef bug (check message.keyword breakdown to separate the two signatures cleanly). 3) Cross-check ki-2026-05-24-runtime-core-rtc-p95-recurring (monitors 115456700/117279738) and its own ES Redis-error check ('Redis operation cancelled'/'Redis operation timed out' on runtime-core-api) in the same window -- per precedence_note, treat co-firing as shared-upstream Redis instability, not two independent incidents. 4) Confirm latency-only: service:tables-fields status:error DD Logs should be near-zero for the Redis-specific cause (the FieldTableNameRef traces are a separate, coincidental signature and DO return non-zero -- don't let them inflate the apparent severity of the Redis story). 5) No Method-side code fix identified -- this looks like a transient Redis-tier connectivity blip (network blip, Redis failover, or ElastiCache maintenance); escalate to infra/DBA-adjacent on-call if it recurs or lasts >5 min, otherwise log and move on. 6) Bump ki-2026-07-02-tables-fields-fieldtablenameref-null-linked-fields separately if its own signature also appears -- do not merge occurrence counts between the two entries.

This is occurrence #26 (backlog catch-up cycle, ~8-day gap since last poll).

Playbook: 1) Confirm synthetic-only: ES aggregate message:'JWT Retrieval Failed' by fields.UserAgent.keyword -- if 100% WindowsPowerShell and 0 real browsers, there is no customer impact; deprioritize. 2) Confirm the NRE: search the same docs for exceptions[].StackTraceString containing GetAccountBySubdomain in Com.Method.ServiceContract/Services/Account/MethodSessionService.cs. 3) Two independent fixes, pick per owner: (a) CODE -- add a null guard in MethodSessionService.GetAccountBySubdomain() so a missing/unknown subdomain returns 400/empty-session instead of dereferencing null (source is TFS-built Com.Method.ServiceContract, NOT in the GitHub clones -- route to the platform-ui/MethodUI backend owner); (b) MONITORING -- fix the Centreon synthetic check to send a valid account subdomain / Host header, or point it at a health endpoint that doesn't require an account, which silences both the false-CRITICAL Centreon alerts and the Datadog Watchdog 236570583 'New issue to review' noise. 4) Establish WHY it started at ~12:51Z (check Centreon check-config change history around that time). 5) Until fixed, #alert-system will keep getting intermittent Centreon CRITICALs + Watchdog 236570583 fires for this pattern -- treat as monitoring noise, not a customer outage.

🚨 *new alert — needs human*  (score: 8)
Channel: alert-system (DD-scan-diff, backlog catch-up)  •  alerts in group: 4
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `admin`

Symptoms:
  - 4 independent P95-latency monitors across Gateway, IdentityAPI, Signin, and AccountAPI all elevated within the same ~8-minute window (12:39-12:47Z), plus a co-timed Synthetics sign-in-navigation monitor (142763851, logged separately as a KI recurrence).
  - ms-gateway-api itself shows the clearest breach (3.79s vs 1.5s threshold) -- gateway proxies all 3 of the other affected services, making it the most plausible shared-upstream cause.
  - Different specific service combination than the existing ki-2026-07-14-cross-service-p95-latency-shared-upstream entry (that one covers miurl/ms-search-api/RTC/classicmethod) -- same causal SHAPE (gateway-adjacent multi-service co-fire), but this is a new, un-catalogued instance a week later.

Likely cause: Transient ms-gateway-api latency spike cascading to p95 latency on 3 services it proxies (Signin, Identity, Account), self-recovered within the ~8-min window.
